title: Cross-language SDK error taxonomy (names + standard fields)
creator: Ibrahim Khan
body:
## Context
We continue to see "works in TS but not Python" class issues where the underlying HTTP response is the same, but SDKs surface different exception types, different field names, and frequently drop request_id. This blocks Support/oncall workflows and makes it hard for customers to implement safe retries and telemetry.

This ticket defines the shared error taxonomy and required fields to be implemented in Python, TypeScript, and Go, and enforced via the cross-language conformance suite.

## Goals
1) Shared *conceptual* taxonomy (same categories) across languages.
2) Shared *field set* on all SDK errors:
   - request_id (string; may be empty if truly unavailable)
   - status_code (int when HTTP response exists)
   - code (string error code enum from API, when present)
   - type (string high-level type: api_error | transport_error | timeout_error | stream_error)
   - retryable (bool)
   - retry_after_ms (int when provided by server via Retry-After or equivalent)
   - raw_message (string from server, redaction-safe)
   - details (string or compact JSON-string; language-specific structured data allowed but MUST NOT include secrets)
3) Deterministic mapping rules from HTTP status + error code -> error class.
4) Conformance tests: golden fixtures for error shapes and retryable classification.
5) Ensure errors are safe to log (no API keys, no Authorization header values, no raw request bodies by default).

## Non-goals
- Introducing new auth mechanisms.
- Redesigning the public API error payload beyond platform’s consistency work (tracked in ENG-5130).
- Forcing identical error *names* across languages (language idioms OK), but categories + required fields MUST match.

## Taxonomy (conceptual)
All SDK errors MUST derive from a single base error type (language-idiomatic):
- Base: RedwoodError
  - message: developer-friendly summary
  - request_id: string ("req_...")
  - type: one of api_error | transport_error | timeout_error | stream_error
  - retryable: boolean
  - status_code: optional int
  - code: optional string (server error code enum)
  - retry_after_ms: optional int

Subclasses / categories (recommended names):

### API / HTTP response errors (type=api_error)
- AuthenticationError
  - Typical: 401, invalid_api_key, missing_auth
  - retryable: false
- PermissionDeniedError
  - Typical: 403
  - retryable: false
- RateLimitError
  - Typical: 429
  - retryable: true (respect Retry-After if present)
- InvalidRequestError
  - Typical: 400, 422 (validation errors)
  - retryable: false
- NotFoundError
  - Typical: 404
  - retryable: false
- ConflictError
  - Typical: 409 (idempotency conflict / state conflict)
  - retryable: false by default (may be context-dependent; do not auto-retry)
- RequestTooLargeError
  - Typical: 413
  - retryable: false
- UnsupportedMediaTypeError
  - Typical: 415
  - retryable: false
- InternalServerError
  - Typical: 500
  - retryable: true
- ServiceUnavailableError
  - Typical: 503
  - retryable: true
- GatewayTimeoutError
  - Typical: 504
  - retryable: true

Note: For 502/503/504, classify as retryable=true.

### Transport / network errors (type=transport_error)
- NetworkError
  - DNS errors, TCP resets, connection refused, TLS handshake failures
  - retryable: true (bounded by standard retry policy)
  - status_code: absent

### Timeout errors (type=timeout_error)
- TimeoutError
  - overall timeout or read timeout / deadline exceeded (depending on language client)
  - retryable: true (bounded)
  - status_code: absent unless timeout occurs after response headers (rare; if present, include)

### Streaming errors (type=stream_error)
- StreamDisconnectedError
  - Raised when streaming response terminates unexpectedly (socket closed mid-chunk, proxy interruption, decompression errors)
  - Must include request_id when known (often from initial response headers)
  - retryable: false by default for auto-retry; guidance is manual retry only with idempotency considerations

## Mapping rules (normative)
Given an HTTP response:
1) Extract request_id from (in priority order):
   - Response header: x-request-id
   - Error payload field: request_id
   - Otherwise empty string
2) Determine retry_after_ms:
   - Parse Retry-After header (seconds or HTTP-date) -> ms until retry, clamp to [0, 120000] for display/use
   - If parsing fails, omit
3) Determine code:
   - Use server error payload field ("code"), if present, else empty
4) Determine class:
   - If status_code == 401 -> AuthenticationError
   - 403 -> PermissionDeniedError
   - 404 -> NotFoundError
   - 409 -> ConflictError
   - 413 -> RequestTooLargeError
   - 415 -> UnsupportedMediaTypeError
   - 422 -> InvalidRequestError
   - 429 -> RateLimitError
   - 500 -> InternalServerError
   - 502/503 -> ServiceUnavailableError (or dedicated BadGatewayError for 502 is OK, but must be retryable)
   - 504 -> GatewayTimeoutError
   - Else 400-499 -> InvalidRequestError (retryable=false)
   - Else 500-599 -> InternalServerError (retryable=true)

For non-HTTP failures:
- Timeout -> TimeoutError
- Network -> NetworkError
- Streaming disconnect -> StreamDisconnectedError

## Standard serialization for logs/telemetry (fields)
Every SDK MUST be able to produce a redaction-safe, structured representation for logging:
- name: error class name
- type: api_error | transport_error | timeout_error | stream_error
- message: string
- request_id: string
- status_code: int or empty
- code: string
- retryable: boolean
- retry_after_ms: int or empty

## Security / privacy notes
- Do not include Authorization header values.
- Do not include full request/response bodies by default.
- Server-provided message is allowed but must be treated as untrusted text; no interpolation of secrets.
- If an SDK offers a debug mode that captures HTTP headers, it must explicitly redact: Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, and any known secret headers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Spec reviewed by SRE + Security + PM (Monica/Allison/Marcus/Henry).
- [x] Python/TS/Go: request_id present on all API errors when gateway provides it.
- [x] retryable flag matches standard for status codes + transport/timeouts.
- [x] Retry-After parsed and exposed as retry_after_ms for 429 (and optionally for 503 where present).
- [x] Conformance suite includes golden fixtures for:
  - 429 with Retry-After seconds + HTTP-date
  - 500/503/504
  - 400/422
  - network error
  - timeout
  - streaming disconnect mid-chunk
- [x] Docs/migration guide references the new error fields.

## Implementation notes by language
### TypeScript
- Maintain exported error classes; ensure they extend a common base (RedwoodError).
- Ensure fetch/AbortController errors are normalized into TimeoutError vs NetworkError.

### Python
- Wrap httpx/requests exceptions and normalize to NetworkError/TimeoutError.
- Streaming iterator should raise StreamDisconnectedError with partial output accessible (if provided by iterator API), but error itself must not embed the full output.

### Go
- net/http errors normalized; context deadline exceeded -> TimeoutError.
- Streaming: read loop must surface disconnect as StreamDisconnectedError; include request_id captured from initial headers.

## Links
- Confluence standard: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/sdk-retry-timeout-standard.json
- Security guidance: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/sdk-auth-resolution-and-secret-handling.json
- Platform dependencies: ENG-5130 (Retry-After + request_id consistency)

Related PRs (implementation):
- TS: redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-1298-unify-retry-middleware-and-error-shapes.json
- Go: redwood-sdk-go/pr-624-streaming-reconnect-guidance-and-error-types.json
- Python: redwood-sdk-python/pr-854-streaming-disconnect-handling-and-errors.json
- Gateway: redwood/pr-28426-standardize-request-id-propagation.json

## Open questions (resolved)
- Should 409 be retryable? => No (default false); document as potentially resolvable by changing request/idempotency usage.
- Should 502 have its own class? => Optional; MUST be retryable and included under api_error.
- Should we expose raw headers? => No by default; only via explicit debug hooks with redaction.
comments: 2026-01-16 — Ibrahim Khan: Drafted initial taxonomy + required fields. Biggest gaps today: TS drops request_id on some non-2xx, Python stream errors don’t always retain request_id, Go doesn’t parse Retry-After.

2026-01-20 — Allison Grant: Please ensure retryable classification is a pure function of (type/status_code/code) so dashboards can aggregate consistently. Add retry_after_ms and clamp behavior; avoid negative durations on date parsing.

2026-01-22 — Marcus Lin: Security review: confirm we never log Authorization; ensure server message is treated as untrusted text. OK with including request_id/status_code/code/retryable in error’s string form as long as API key is never interpolated.

2026-01-27 — Henry Cho: Product request: keep names stable where possible to minimize breaking changes; include migration note for TS users currently checking `err.status` or `err.response.status` directly.

2026-02-03 — Dana Lo: TS implementation in progress (PR-1298). Normalizing AbortError vs network errors was tricky; will map AbortError from our internal timeout path to TimeoutError; external aborts (user cancel) should produce a distinct cancellation reason but still be a StreamDisconnectedError for streaming.
2026-02-07 — Mateusz Zielinski: Go streaming: capturing request_id requires reading initial headers before starting event loop. Implemented; added tests for mid-stream FIN and proxy-induced EOF.
2026-02-12 — Sabrina James: Python: made StreamDisconnectedError include request_id when available from initial response; ensured error __str__ includes request_id/status_code but not response body.

2026-02-18 — Ibrahim Khan: Conformance fixtures added for 429 Retry-After (seconds + date) and a golden error JSON shape. Remaining: ensure gateway always sets x-request-id on streaming errors (tracked in ENG-5130).
2026-02-24 — Connor O'Brien: Marking Done after signoff. Release coordination will ensure migration notes call out new fields and any renamed error classes per SDK.
